questions.q: What does Claude's response look like when it calls more than one tool in a single turn?
options: The API returns an error, since only one tool call is allowed per turn
A single tool_use block that lists multiple tool names inside it
A content array containing multiple separate tool_use blocks, each with its own id
Two completely separate API responses sent simultaneously
questions.explain: By default, Claude may call multiple tools in one response — the content array simply contains more than one tool_use block, each independently identified.

questions.q: Per Anthropic's current documentation, what are the formatting rules for responding to multiple tool_use blocks from one turn?
options: Only the first tool_result needs to be sent; the rest are optional
Return one tool_result for each tool_use block, all together in the next user message, matched by tool_use_id, with all tool_results before any text
Send each tool_result in its own separate API request
Tool results can be sent in any message, at any later point in the conversation
questions.explain: Every tool_use block from that turn needs a matching tool_result, grouped together in the following user message, with results ordered before any text content.

questions.q: Does the Claude API require you to run multiple requested tool calls concurrently?
options: Yes, the API only works if all calls are executed as true parallel operations
Yes, but only when using a specific experimental API flag
No, sequential execution is strictly forbidden by the API
No — the API doesn't prescribe execution order; concurrent vs. sequential is your application's decision based on what the tools actually do
questions.explain: Independent, read-only operations are often safe to run concurrently for lower latency; tools with side effects or ordering dependencies may be safer run one at a time — that choice is yours.

questions.q: If a tool call is never actually executed (e.g., skipped after an earlier call in the same batch failed), what does this lesson say you must still do?
options: Simply omit any tool_result for that tool_use id
Send a completely new tools array with that tool removed
Restart the entire conversation from the first user message
Still return a tool_result for it, with is_error: true and a brief explanation like 'not executed'
questions.explain: Every tool_use id from that turn needs a matching result, even for calls you chose not to run — the documented pattern is is_error: true with a short explanation.

questions.q: Why might an agent request get_weather and get_traffic for the same location in one turn instead of looping twice?
options: Because the two sub-goals are independent of each other's results, so there's no reason to wait for one before requesting the other
Because the Claude API requires at least two tool calls in every turn
Because get_weather and get_traffic are actually the same tool with two names
Because looping twice is always technically impossible
questions.explain: Unlike Lesson 2's weather/ticket example where the second call needed the first call's result, weather and traffic for the same place don't depend on each other — so both can be requested at once.
